title: TCA overdose: ECG, bicarbonate and decontamination
stem: Resus 2. A 40-year-old woman (about 70 kg) on treatment for depression was found drowsy at home by her husband, who last saw her well an hour ago. An empty packet of amitriptyline 25 mg (60 tablets) was beside her. GCS E2 V2 M3, HR 120, BP 90/40, RR 10, SpO2 90% on room air. A 12-lead ECG is on the trolley.

phases.title: Arrival
phases.goal: Take charge: call the team and the kit you will need, get your gloves on, and read the packet. What, how much, and when?

phases.title: ABC
phases.goal: Get the nurse to put her on the monitor, oxygen and access. Examine her yourself, A to E. Say whether the airway is protected, and what you will not do yet.

phases.title: ECG
phases.goal: Read the 12-lead before any drug and treat what it shows, promptly. Get ready for VT. Treat anything that happens to her, then repeat the ECG.

phases.title: RSI
phases.goal: Kit from the trolley, drugs from the cart, then intubate her yourself once the bicarbonate is in. Set the ventilator yourself for this poisoning.

phases.title: Circulation
phases.goal: Still hypotensive? Treat it from the drug cart, with the right dose.

phases.title: Decontamination and labs
phases.goal: Now the airway is safe: decide on charcoal and lavage, and send the bloods that matter.

phases.title: Close
phases.goal: Call the people who need to know. Then the examiner will come for your plan and questions.

review.text: Gastric lavage window. Your older notes extend lavage to about 4 hours for anticholinergic drugs. International guidance (AACT/EAPCCT), and your own perfect script, say lavage is not first-line: only for a life-threatening ingestion with tablets likely still in the stomach, a protected airway, and HKPIC and a senior agreeing.
Charcoal 'down the tube'. Your script says charcoal 50 g down the tube after intubation. Say which tube: it goes down an orogastric or nasogastric tube, never the endotracheal tube.

Seizure dose. Your script gives midazolam 1–2 mg IV, a sedation-sized dose. For a seizure give lorazepam 4 mg IV (0.1 mg/kg), or midazolam titrated at about 0.1 mg/kg (for example 5 mg IV, repeated), with another bicarbonate bolus.

notes:
Checked against TOXBASE, the Hong Kong Poison Information Centre (HKPIC) guidance, and the AACT/EAPCCT position papers on gastric lavage (2013) and activated charcoal. The station follows your perfect script.

Tricyclics block fast sodium channels (broad QRS, VT), alpha receptors (hypotension), muscarinic receptors (tachycardia, dilated pupils, retention, delayed gastric emptying) and cause seizures. QRS over 100 ms predicts seizures; over 160 ms predicts arrhythmias. A terminal R wave in aVR over 3 mm is another marker.

Order: call the team and read the pack; ABC with monitoring, access, gas and glucose, and say the airway is not protected (no charcoal or lavage yet); read the ECG before other drugs; sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 1–2 mmol/kg (50–100 mL in an adult) as a rapid bolus, repeated for persistent QRS widening, VT or shock, then a repeat ECG; RSI after the bicarbonate, because the apnoeic pause causes acidosis that widens the QRS; then hyperventilate to pH 7.45–7.55. Hypotension: crystalloid 500–1000 mL, then noradrenaline. VT once the pH is 7.5: lignocaine 1–1.5 mg/kg. Seizures: benzodiazepines plus more bicarbonate. Avoid amiodarone and class Ia/Ic drugs, phenytoin, flumazenil and physostigmine.

Decontamination: activated charcoal 50 g via an orogastric or nasogastric tube once the airway is protected, within about an hour of a life-threatening dose. Gastric lavage is not first-line (AACT/EAPCCT): only if HKPIC and a senior agree tablets are still in the stomach. Bloods: gas, electrolytes, glucose, paracetamol; do not wait for a TCA level. Disposition: HKPIC and ICU. An alert patient with a normal ECG is monitored for 6 hours from ingestion, then referred to psychiatry.

steps.label: Take charge
steps.hint: Announce yourself; call the resus team with airway kit, suction and the defibrillator.

opts.t: I am the AED doctor. Resus team please: airway trolley, suction, defibrillator.
opts.mark: Takes charge and calls the team, airway kit, suction and defibrillator

opts.t: Start with a full history from the husband before touching her
opts.r: She is shocked, hypoxic and GCS 7. Resuscitate first; the history comes from the packet and the door note.

steps.label: Trolley
steps.hint: Gloves before you touch her.

opts.t: Gloves and apron
opts.mark: Gloves and apron on

steps.label: The packet
steps.hint: Read the empty packet beside her.

Scene.r: Amitriptyline 25 mg, 60 tablets, all gone: up to 1.5 g. Her husband left her well an hour ago. GCS 7, shocked and hypoxic: life-threatening TCA poisoning.
Scene.mark: Identifies the drug, the dose and the time: life-threatening TCA poisoning

steps.label: Monitoring and access
steps.hint: Ask the nurse for monitoring, oxygen and access. Tell the team the airway is not protected.

opts.t: Put her on the monitor: ECG leads, NIBP cuff and SpO2 probe.
opts.mark: Asks for continuous ECG, NIBP and SpO2 monitoring

opts.t: Non-rebreather mask at 15 L/min.
opts.mark: High-flow oxygen

opts.t: Two large-bore cannulae, bloods and a venous gas.
opts.mark: Two large-bore IVs, bloods and a gas

opts.t: Her airway is not protected. I am planning RSI. No charcoal and no lavage tube yet.
opts.mark: States the airway is unprotected: plans RSI, no charcoal or lavage yet

steps.label: Examine
steps.hint: Hands on, A to E: airway, breathing, circulation, pupils and GCS, glucose, then expose.

A–B.r: Snoring. Tongue falling back. Gag weak. Airway not protected.
RR 10, shallow. Equal air entry, chest clear. SpO2 90% on air.

C.r: Pulse 120, regular, thready. Capillary refill 3 s. Skin warm, dry and flushed.

D.r: Pupils 6 mm, sluggish. GCS E2 V2 M3 = 7.

E.r: Dry flushed skin, palpable bladder, quiet bowel sounds. No injuries, no other packets.

steps.label: 12-lead ECG
steps.hint: Open the 12-lead. Rate, QRS width, aVR.

opts.t: Sinus tachycardia, QRS over 100 ms, tall terminal R in aVR: sodium-channel blockade.
opts.mark: Reads the ECG: broad QRS and tall R in aVR, sodium-channel blockade

opts.t: Broad complex tachycardia: VT. Amiodarone 300 mg.
opts.r: P waves before every QRS: sinus tachycardia with a broad QRS. Amiodarone adds to the cardiotoxicity.

opts.t: Tall tented T waves: hyperkalaemia. Calcium first.
opts.r: Look again: the T waves are not peaked. The QRS is broad with a tall R in aVR — sodium-channel blockade.

opts.t: Sinus tachycardia with a normal QRS. Reassuring.
opts.r: The QRS is about 140 ms, with a tall terminal R in aVR. This predicts seizures and arrhythmias.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Treat the broad QRS before anything else.

opts.t: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 100 mL (1–2 mmol/kg) rapid IV
opts.mark: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 1–2 mmol/kg rapid bolus for the broad QRS

opts.t: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 25 mL IV
opts.r: Too little. 1–2 mmol/kg: 50–100 mL of 8.4% in an adult, as a rapid bolus.

opts.t: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 500 mL IV over 10 minutes
opts.r: Too much at once: hypernatraemia and severe alkalaemia. Give 50–100 mL boluses titrated to the QRS and pH.

opts.t: Amiodarone 300 mg IV
opts.r: Amiodarone prolongs the QT and adds to the cardiotoxicity. Bicarbonate first; lignocaine only for VT once the pH is 7.5.

opts.t: Flumazenil 200 micrograms IV
opts.r: Flumazenil can precipitate seizures and arrhythmias in TCA overdose.

opts.t: Physostigmine 1 mg IV
opts.r: Contraindicated in TCA poisoning: asystole has occurred.

opts.t: Phenytoin 20 mg/kg IV
opts.r: Phenytoin blocks sodium channels too and can worsen cardiotoxicity. Benzodiazepines only.

opts.t: Flecainide 2 mg/kg IV
opts.r: Class Ic: more sodium-channel block. Avoid class Ia and Ic drugs in TCA poisoning.

opts.t: Lignocaine 1.5 mg/kg IV
opts.r: She is not in VT. Lignocaine is for VT that persists once the pH is 7.5.

opts.t: Noradrenaline infusion 0.1 microgram/kg/min
opts.r: Not yet: bicarbonate and fluid first. Noradrenaline is for hypotension that persists after them.

steps.label: Trolley
steps.hint: VT is coming: be ready to shock.

opts.t: Defibrillator pads on the chest
opts.mark: Defibrillator pads on in case of VT

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: She is fitting: a benzodiazepine, and more bicarbonate.

opts.t: Lorazepam 4 mg IV
Lorazepam 0.5 mg IV
opts.r: Too little to stop a seizure: 4 mg IV (0.1 mg/kg), repeated once if needed.

opts.t: Lorazepam 10 mg IV
opts.r: Too much in one go: 4 mg IV, repeated once if needed.

opts.t: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 100 mL (1–2 mmol/kg) rapid IV
opts.early: Watch what the ECG does first.

steps.label: Repeat ECG
steps.hint: After the bicarbonate: has the QRS narrowed?

opts.t: After bicarbonate the QRS has narrowed to about 100 ms and the rate is slower. Keep the pH 7.45–7.55.
opts.mark: Repeats the ECG and sees the QRS narrow
opts.early: The bicarbonate is not in yet.

steps.label: Trolley
steps.hint: Intubation kit.

opts.t: Intubation kit: laryngoscope, size 7.0 tube, bougie, suction, capnography
opts.mark: Prepares the intubation kit with capnography

opts.t: Large-bore lavage tube (36–40 Fr) and funnel
opts.r: Lavage is not first-line. Only if HKPIC and a senior agree tablets are still in the stomach.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Induction that keeps the pressure up, and a relaxant.

opts.t: Ketamine 70 mg IV (1 mg/kg, reduced for shock)
opts.dose: 70 mg IV (1 mg/kg, reduced for shock)
opts.mark: Ketamine, reduced for shock

opts.t: Ketamine 200 mg IV (3 mg/kg)
opts.r: Too much for induction in a shocked patient: about 1 mg/kg.

opts.t: Rocuronium 85 mg IV (1.2 mg/kg)
opts.mark: Rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg for RSI

opts.t: Rocuronium 20 mg IV (0.3 mg/kg)
opts.r: Too little for RSI: 1.2 mg/kg for fast intubating conditions.

opts.t: Propofol 140 mg IV (2 mg/kg)
opts.r: A full dose of propofol in a shocked patient with a BP of 90/40 risks arrest. Ketamine, reduced.

steps.label: Intubate
steps.hint: The bicarbonate is in: now intubate.

Airway.t: Intubate: laryngoscope, tube through the cords, cuff up, capnography
Airway.r: Grade 1 view. 7.0 tube at 21 cm. ETCO2 trace on every breath.
Airway.mark: Intubates after the bicarbonate and confirms with capnography
Airway.early: The bicarbonate is not in yet: the apnoea of RSI would acidify her and widen the QRS.

steps.label: Ventilator
steps.hint: Set it yourself: a controlled mode, 6–8 mL/kg, a faster rate to keep her alkaline.

opts.t: Set the ventilator
opts.performHint: She is paralysed, 70 kg, and must stay alkaline (pH 7.45–7.55). Mode, O2, VT and RR, then PEEP and Pmax. START.
mark: FiO2 100% with PEEP 5 and a pressure limit

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Hypotension: fluid.

opts.t: Crystalloid 500–1000 mL bolus
opts.mark: Crystalloid 500–1000 mL for hypotension

opts.t: Crystalloid 100 mL
opts.r: Too little to treat hypotension: 500–1000 mL, then reassess.

opts.t: Crystalloid 3 L as fast as possible
opts.r: Too much without reassessment: 500–1000 mL, then reassess; bicarbonate is the main treatment.

steps.label: Trolley
steps.hint: A way into the stomach, now the airway is safe.

opts.t: Orogastric tube, placed and checked
opts.mark: Orogastric tube once the airway is protected

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: About an hour, a life-threatening load, airway protected.

opts.t: Activated charcoal 50 g down the orogastric tube
opts.early: Her airway is not protected yet.
opts.mark: Activated charcoal 50 g via the orogastric tube

opts.t: Activated charcoal 10 g
opts.r: Too little: 50 g (about 1 g/kg) in an adult.

opts.t: Activated charcoal 200 g
opts.r: Too much: 50 g (about 1 g/kg) in an adult.

steps.label: Lavage?
steps.hint: Say what you will and will not do about the stomach.

opts.t: No lavage now. Only if HKPIC and a senior agree tablets are still in the stomach; delayed emptying is a discussion, not a four-hour rule.
opts.mark: Lavage only if HKPIC and a senior agree: not routine

steps.label: Bloods
steps.hint: What you send, and what you do not wait for.

opts.t: Send the gas, electrolytes, glucose and a paracetamol level. We are not waiting for a TCA level.
opts.mark: Gas, electrolytes, glucose and paracetamol; does not wait for a TCA level

opts.t: Send a TCA level and hold treatment until it is back
opts.r: TCA levels do not guide emergency treatment. Treat the ECG and the patient.

steps.label: Phone
steps.hint: Poison centre and ICU.

opts.t: Hong Kong Poison Information Centre (at United Christian Hospital) via the operator
opts.mark: Calls the Hong Kong Poison Information Centre

opts.t: ICU: intubated TCA overdose, bicarbonate given, charcoal after the tube
opts.mark: Refers to ICU with a clear handover

steps.label: Your plan
steps.ask: Tell me where she goes and how you would have managed her if she had been well.
steps.hint: Disposition, the well-patient pathway, and documentation.

opts.t: She goes to ICU. Had she been alert with a normal ECG, I would monitor for 6 hours from ingestion, then refer to psychiatry.
opts.mark: ICU; an alert patient with a normal ECG is monitored 6 hours, then psychiatry

opts.t: I document the times, and the ECGs before and after bicarbonate.
opts.mark: Documents times and the pre- and post-bicarbonate ECGs

opts.t: Physostigmine once she is on ICU to wake her up
opts.r: Physostigmine is contraindicated in TCA poisoning: asystole has occurred.

qs.q: QRS duration that predicts seizures in TCA poisoning?

qs.a: Apnoea causes acidosis and widens the QRS
wrong: Bicarbonate is a better induction agent
It shortens the action of the relaxant
It stops the gag reflex returning

qs.q: VT persists despite bicarbonate at pH 7.5. Next?
Still hypotensive after bicarbonate and 1 L of fluid?
She seizes. Which drug, and which to avoid?

rules.fail: Drugs were given before the ECG was read.
rules.ok: The ECG was read before other drugs.

rules.fail: The ECG was repeated before any bicarbonate: nothing had changed yet.
Intubated before the bicarbonate: the apnoeic pause worsens the sodium-channel block.
A tube or charcoal into the stomach before the airway was protected.
Touched her before gloves were on.

badge.name: Salt of the Earth
badge.flavor: Read the ECG, bicarbonate before the tube, charcoal after it.

cards.q: First drug for TCA overdose with QRS 140 ms and hypotension?
cards.why: Sodium load and alkalinisation reverse sodium-channel blockade.

cards.q: ECG sign in aVR suggesting sodium-channel blockade?
options: A deep Q wave over 3 mm

cards.q: Gastric lavage tube size in adults?
cards.why: Large bore to pass tablet fragments.
Keeps the pylorus up and reduces aspiration.

cards.q: Activated charcoal is most useful within…
cards.why: Later use may be considered for delayed-release or anticholinergic drugs.

events.say: She is fitting: a generalised tonic–clonic seizure. SpO2 falling.
events.untreated: She fitted and never got a benzodiazepine.

events.say: As you reach the bed she starts fitting: a generalised tonic–clonic seizure.
events.untreated: She fitted and never got a benzodiazepine.
